title: Canonical payload check run
statement: Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean, let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $x,b,$ and $t$ be Boolean words. Let $v$ assign each of the fourteen registers a natural number at most $B$, with register $3$ equal to twice the length of the encoding of $x$ paired with $b$, and register $4$ equal to $4|x|+4$. Then there is a register assignment $v'$, also bounded by $B$, that agrees with $v$ on every register other than register $0$, such that the abstract machine, starting in the canonicality-check state on the input encoding of the pair whose first component is the encoding of $x$ paired with $b$ and whose second component is $t$, reaches the inner-preparation state if $b$ is canonical and otherwise the negative-answer state, with no answer recorded; throughout the run, the prescribed configuration invariant holds.
